alex.k: Heads-up: provisioning conversation for ACME Corp Dedicated pool. They want ~200 rps of gen traffic split EU/US, multi-tenant, contract requires 99.9% uptime and p95 latency <200ms. How should we size reserved GPUs and what buffer for bursty tenants? Also thoughts on egress billing impact? cc @tara_infra @cheng_runtime @priya_finance

tara_infra: Quick clarifying q: is 200 rps sustained or peak? need request length distribution and % embeddings vs gen. sustained 200 rps with avg 40 tokens is very different than 200 rps peak with 1k spikes.

cheng_runtime: From our benches: a system with A40-like perf gives ~120 tokens/sec for the target model mix (chat+gen). So rough calc: requests_per_gpu = gpu_tokens_per_sec / avg_tokens_per_request. For avg 40 tokens => ~3 rps per GPU. So 200 rps => ~67 GPUs. Add safety (cache misses, tail latency, simultaneous KV loads) => recommend 1.4-1.6x => ~95-110 GPUs.

cheng_runtime: Formula I used: 
```
required_gpus = ceil((target_rps * avg_tokens_per_req) / gpu_tokens_per_sec * safety_factor)
```

priya_finance: Important to get accurate price per GPU/hr. Using a rough price of $2.8/hr (example cloud family) for est: 100 GPUs * $2.8 * 24 * 30 ~= $201k/month (compute only). Egress can add a lot depending on embedding rates and response sizes. If ACME sends a lot of embeddings (or stores logs) estimate 10-50TB/mo at $0.08/GB => additional $8k-$40k/mo.

jon_sre: From infra side: avoid cross-region fallbacks because egress + cross-AZ latency kills p95. Recommend region-pref routing: EU traffic served by EU pool, US by US pool, with local burst capacity. Also we should enforce model-variant fallback (smaller quantized model) before cross-region routing.

ops-bot: Capacity-sim job queued: job #352 for ACME request profile. ETA ~2h. Results link: https://internal/ci/sim/352

tara_infra: Operational approach: create 3 tenant profiles: steady (long-lived baseline), bursty (short <=30s peaks), and spike (rare multi-second spikes). For steady tenants allocate baseline fractional slots (slot-sharing), for bursty allow ephemeral burst pool up to 1.5x baseline. That reduces committed GPUs while keeping SLA for steady workloads.

alex.k: Good. Region split idea? If ACME is ~60% EU / 40% US, we should allocate roughly 60/40 of the reserved capacity but keep a small cross-region buffer for failover (but priced as separate).

cheng_runtime: Another lever: KV cache prewarm. If product can provide top prompt prefixes we see ~10-15% reduction in GPU needs on typical mixes. Also batching latency vs throughput tradeoff: continuous batching helps throughput but raises tail at low qps.

priya_finance: I'll run a tidy spreadsheet with three scenarios (conservative/expected/optimistic) using real GPU/hr numbers and egress tiers, plus amortized support/ops margin. Will post by EOD. If we target 90 GPUs at $2.8/hr => monthly ~181k compute; add average egress 25TB => ~21k egress => ~202k total.

jon_sre: Action items: 1) tara draft reserve plan with region split + tenant profiles, 2) cheng run cache sim + validate GPU tokens/sec number, 3) priya publish cost scenarios, 4) I will validate routing configs + egress limits and add fallback policy to infra playbook.

alex.k: Sounds good. T+48h sync to lock numbers. :thumbsup:
